newsitem.title: USA: CHX to allow stock trading in 16ths increments.
newsitem.headline: CHX to allow stock trading in 16ths increments.

text.p: The Chicago Stock Exchange (CHX) said on Wednesday that it was reducing the minimum trading increments to 16ths for all stocks issued on the New York Stock Exchange and traded in Chicago.
The exchange said it planned to finish upgrading its trading system to enable trading in that increment by June 30.
The CHX said that the minimum trading increment for stocks issued in New York and traded on its exchange used to be in eighths.
"We believe that our ...decision to reduce trading increments will help retain the record trade volumes that our exchange is experiencing this year," it said.
"Year-to-date volume is currently up 18.5 percent over the same period of our record trading year in 1996," CHX added
The CHX is the second largest exchange in the United States, trading more than 4,000 stocks issued on the NYSE, American Stock Exchange, Nasdaq Stock Market and its own exchange.
